reasons.realCost: Notion's real bills at the three sizes ($0, $60 and $180 a month) equal exactly the per-seat plan price times seat count, with no usage overage baked into the organize layer's core docs and database use.
reasons.pricingHonesty: All four plans list per-seat monthly and yearly prices on the pricing page, and the only paid usage add-on, Notion credits for Custom Agents on Business/Enterprise, is priced at $10 per 1,000 credits, though the price of a custom Notion-site domain and Enterprise's quote are not published.
reasons.smallTeamFit: Notion's page-and-database model is widely adopted by non-technical teams for wikis and light project tracking without a developer, though building custom database views, subtasks and dependencies has a learning curve.
reasons.doesTheJob: Notion covers docs, wikis and lightweight databases with subtasks and dependencies well, but has no native Gantt chart, deep automation engine or time tracking, features dedicated project-management tools include.
reasons.freedomToLeave: Notion bills month-to-month by default, supports self-serve export of all workspace content as HTML, Markdown or CSV at any time, and simply lets paid features run out at the end of the billing cycle after cancellation.
reasons.trackRecord: Notion, founded in 2013, publishes an official status page and lists every plan's per-seat price and yearly discount on its public pricing page.

basis: Notion is a strong buy for a small business's organize layer because its per-seat pricing is fully public and predictable, billing is flexible with full self-serve export, though deeper AI features and admin controls require moving to the Business or Enterprise plan.
method: Two independent blind passes scored six factors (1–5) and an overall; published overall is the lower of the two overall scores, because this tool runs an affiliate program we have joined or may join. Pass scores: 4.2 and 4.3.
